phrases.explanation: The Prophet is not responsible for those who divide their faith and form sects. The verse relieves him of control over every group and its choices, without praising division or forbidding thoughtful difference.

phrases.translation: Their judgment rests only with Allah.
phrases.explanation: The judgment of those who divide their faith rests with Allah alone. This places final accountability with God and cautions people against claiming complete authority over others’ standing before Him.

phrases.translation: And He will inform them of what they used to do
phrases.explanation: Allah will inform them of what they used to do. The verse reminds every group that actions remain answerable, even when people disagree about belief or try to claim exclusive moral authority.

phrases.translation: Whoever comes with a good deed will be rewarded tenfold.
phrases.explanation: A person who comes with a good deed is rewarded tenfold. The verse emphasizes the generosity of divine reward, encouraging good action while recognizing that Allah grants more than a simple return.

phrases.translation: But whoever comes with a bad deed will be punished for only one.
phrases.explanation: A bad deed is punished only once, the verse says. The contrast highlights mercy and proportion. Punishment is not multiplied beyond the wrong a person actually committed, and each deed is judged fairly.

phrases.translation: None will be wronged
phrases.explanation: No one will be wronged. The closing affirms fairness in judgment, assuring people that good is not lost and punishment is not increased beyond what each person deserves in Allah’s final accounting.

phrases.translation: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Surely my Lord has guided me to the Straight Path,
phrases.explanation: The Prophet declares that Allah guided him to the Straight Path. Guidance is presented as a gift from God, and the phrase links the Prophet’s mission with the central message of the surah.

phrases.translation: a perfect way, the faith of Abraham, the upright,
phrases.explanation: The path is identified with the upright faith of Abraham. His example links the Prophet’s message to earlier monotheistic guidance and a steadfast rejection of idolatry through genuine worship of Allah alone.

phrases.translation: who was not one of the polytheists.”
phrases.explanation: Abraham was not one of the polytheists. The verse honors his commitment to worshipping Allah alone and rejects attempts to claim him for beliefs that contradict his monotheistic devotion and example.

phrases.translation: Say, “Surely my prayer, my worship, my life, and my death are all for Allah—
phrases.explanation: The Prophet says that his prayer, worship, life, and death are all for Allah. The declaration expresses comprehensive devotion, extending beyond ritual into daily choices and the whole course of life.

phrases.translation: Lord of all worlds
phrases.explanation: Allah is the Lord of all worlds. This grounds the Prophet’s devotion in Allah’s universal sovereignty, extending beyond any single people or place to all creation and every generation, without exception.

phrases.translation: He has no partner.
phrases.explanation: Allah has no partner. This concise statement reinforces the oneness underlying the surah’s teachings about worship and sacrifice, rejecting any claim that another being shares Allah’s divine authority or status.

phrases.translation: So I am commanded, and so I am the first to submit.”
phrases.explanation: The Prophet is commanded to submit and says he is the first to do so. His example presents submission as wholehearted obedience to Allah, not merely a verbal profession of belief.

phrases.translation: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Should I seek a lord other than Allah while He is the Lord of everything?”
phrases.explanation: The Prophet is asked whether he should seek a lord other than Allah, who is Lord of everything. The question rejects rival objects of worship and affirms God’s universal authority.

phrases.translation: No one will reap except what they sow.
phrases.explanation: Each person reaps only what they sow. The image connects actions with consequences and rejects shifting responsibility to someone else. No person can be blamed for another’s choices before Allah.

phrases.translation: No soul burdened with sin will bear the burden of another.
phrases.explanation: No soul burdened with sin bears another’s burden. The verse affirms individual accountability, but does not deny that people can influence one another, offer support in life, or share practical responsibilities during hardship.

phrases.translation: Then to your Lord is your return,
phrases.explanation: Everyone’s return is to Allah. The reminder places human life within a larger horizon of judgment and calls people to reflect on their choices before standing before their Lord at judgment.

phrases.translation: and He will inform you of your differences
phrases.explanation: Allah will inform people of their differences. He knows what they disputed and why, so the verse leaves final resolution to divine knowledge rather than human claims of perfect judgment.

phrases.translation: He is the One Who has placed you as successors on earth
phrases.explanation: Allah has placed people as successors on earth. The role carries responsibility for the world and its communities, not merely a licence to use the earth without care or accountability.

phrases.translation: and elevated some of you in rank over others,
phrases.explanation: People differ in rank and circumstance. The verse describes variation in what people have been given, not an automatic measure of human worth or permission to mistreat those with less.

phrases.translation: so He may test you with what He has given you.
phrases.explanation: Differences in provision are a test. People are accountable for how they use their gifts and opportunities, including whether they respond with gratitude, fairness, and care for others rather than using them selfishly.

phrases.translation: Surely your Lord is swift in punishment, but He is certainly All-Forgiving, Most Merciful
phrases.explanation: Allah is swift in punishment, yet All-Forgiving and Most Merciful. This closing balances warning with hope: people should take responsibility, repent sincerely, and trust in Allah’s mercy when they turn back.
